cards.text: The LORD has a word for Moses. This one's about who stays inside the camp and who has to be sent outside. Listen close, friend, because God is VERY specific here.

cards.question: The LORD tells Moses to send certain people away from the camp. Which of these is one of them?

cards.text: Skin disease is one group. The other two are anyone with a bodily discharge and anyone defiled by a dead body.

cards.question: The LORD says only the men with a skin disease, a discharge or defilement from a dead body have to be sent outside the camp.
Why does the LORD want anyone with a skin disease, a discharge or defilement from a dead body sent outside the camp?

answers.text: So the camp where God lives isn't defiled
So the camp's tribes can march in order
So the camp's Levites can finish counting

cards.question: When the LORD gives this command, the Israelites do just as He instructed Moses.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses again. New topic: what happens when a man or woman sins against another person.

cards.question: When someone sins against another person, they act unfaithfully against the ___.
That person is guilty. What's the first thing the guilty person must do?

answers.text: Leave the camp for a week

cards.question: After confessing, he must make full restitution. What does he add on top of it?
When a guilty person confesses, the full restitution plus a fifth goes to the person he wronged.

cards.text: So knock five cookies off my counter, and you owe me SIX. But here's a curveball, friend: what if there's no relative who can receive the restitution?

cards.question: With no relative to pay back, the restitution belongs to the ___.
When there's no relative to receive it, the restitution is given to the priest along with a ram of atonement.

cards.text: Then the LORD adds one last word, about the sacred gifts the Israelites bring to the priest.

cards.question: Every sacred contribution the Israelites bring to the priest belongs to ___.
Before a man gives his sacred gifts to the priest, they still belong to the man.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin's voice barely shows up. The only real joke is on card 12. Story cards 3, 7 and 15 are plain summaries with no personality, and card 1's 'God is VERY specific here' is just pleasant. Moments like people being sent outside the camp, or a guilty person having to confess, could each hold a real laugh without muddying a fact.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: Card 3 is a bare list of the other two groups ('Skin disease is one group. The other two are...'). It has none of Papa Dorin's voice.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: Card 15 is a flat transition line with no voice. It only names the topic of verse 9.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.

findings.problem: The question says 'defilement from a dead body.' The right answer is the only one that echoes it ('isn't defiled') and the only one that mentions God. The two wrong answers (tribes marching in order, Levites counting) have nothing to do with the three groups. The right answer stands out at a glance.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The question says the contributions are brought 'to the priest,' and the right answer is 'the priest.' The wording of the question rules out 'the Levites' and 'the elders,' so the answer is given away instead of reasoned out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'camp' is not the same kind of thing as 'LORD' and 'priests.' Something you act unfaithfully against should be a person or persons, and 'camp' is a place.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
